meta.note: Values below are representative handbook/typical-batch figures (comparable to MMPDS, MatWeb, and standard aerospace materials references), not a specific mill certification. Real properties vary by heat treatment, batch, test temperature, and manufacturer -- verify against a datasheet before citing an exact number to a HAL panel. All values room-temperature unless otherwise noted.

key_mechanical_properties.note: 0-degree = along fiber direction (unidirectional layup); off-axis/quasi-isotropic properties are substantially lower -- see quasi-isotropic entry below.

items.garun_relevance: The most cost-effective composite reference point if the panel asks about material cost trade-offs behind your C_D0/weight assumptions (§5.2, §5.9) -- lower performance than T800/IM7 but significantly cheaper.
items.description: The oldest and most widely available standard-modulus aerospace carbon fiber; still common for secondary (non-flight-critical) structures where cost matters more than peak performance.

typical_aerospace_applications: Primary wing/fuselage structure (e.g. Boeing 787-class primary structure)
items.garun_relevance: The realistic material class behind your blueprint's claimed L/D=16-with-C_D0=0.025-and-AR=8 inconsistency (§5.2/Part 14) -- a genuinely purpose-designed T800-class composite airfoil is one legitimate way to justify better-than-baseline aerodynamic assumptions if paired with an actual airfoil selection.
items.description: A step up from T300 in both strength and stiffness; representative of the fiber class used in modern primary composite airframe structures.

items.type: Intermediate-modulus carbon fiber, toughened epoxy matrix
items.garun_relevance: The single most-cited composite system in published aerospace structural literature -- the strongest choice if your Assumptions Appendix (Appendix A) needs one well-documented, defensible composite reference for the 'Structural weight fraction' row.
items.description: One of the most extensively characterized and published aerospace prepreg systems (Hexcel 8552 matrix); a toughened epoxy specifically formulated for damage tolerance in primary structure, widely used as the benchmark system in composite-structures research.

items.material: Quasi-Isotropic Laminate, generic (e.g. [0/+45/-45/90]s stacking, IM7/8552-class fiber)

key_mechanical_properties.note: These in-plane values are what you should actually use for a real component-level structural estimate -- unidirectional 0-degree properties (see other entries) never apply directly to a real panel, which always carries multi-angle plies to resist loads from more than one direction.

typical_aerospace_applications: Real wing skins, fuselage panels -- i.e. what an actual built structure looks like, as opposed to a single-direction test coupon
items.garun_relevance: IMPORTANT: if you ever quote a composite 'strength' number to a HAL panel, this entry -- not the unidirectional entries above -- is the honest one to use for a component-level claim. Citing a 0-degree unidirectional number (1500-2800 MPa) as if it applied to your whole airframe would be a significant and easily-caught overstatement.
items.description: Roughly a quarter to a third of the unidirectional fiber-direction strength/stiffness, because only a fraction of the fibers in a real multi-angle laminate are aligned with any given load direction -- this is the number a structural reviewer will actually expect to see.
